subject: Dedicated capacity — ops criteria confirmation & next steps (Finexa)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Rios <daniel.rios@finexa.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — ops criteria confirmation & next steps (Finexa)

Hi Daniel / Finexa ops team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear overview of your traffic patterns and the pain you're seeing. Below is a brief recap from our side to make sure we captured the priorities and to align on next steps. If anything is off or missing, please flag and we'll update.

Summary of what we heard (pain points):
- Latency spikes during daily peak windows (08:00–11:00 PT) causing timeouts for synchronous features (p95 occasionally > 900ms).
- Cost unpredictability on bursty embedding workloads — current vendor auto-scale sometimes overprovisions GPUs for short spikes.
- Data isolation & compliance concerns: Finexa must keep PII-inferred payloads on dedicated hardware and have audit logs for access.
- Cold-start variability for model-backed features after weekend traffic drop.

Current stack & constraints:
- Inference: in-house model serving using Triton + Kubernetes, with a managed caching layer for frequent prompts.
- Orchestration: CI/CD for model artifacts; JWT-based auth to endpoints.
- SLOs: interactive features target p95 < 200ms; batch embeddings can tolerate higher latency but need throughput guarantees.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit (what Finexa told us):
1) Predictable throughput: sustained 250 RPS for chat endpoints during peak with ability to burst to 500 RPS for up to 30 minutes.
2) Latency: p95 < 200ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) under expected load profile.
3) Isolation: dedicated GPU pool (no shared tenancy) and customer-managed encrypted storage for logs/artifacts.
4) Autoscale and burst: scale-up within ~90 seconds for planned events; automatic fallback to lower-cost variant if primary capacity is exhausted.
5) Operational observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and traceable audit logs for each request.

Attachments I referenced on the call:
- finexa-inference-telemetry-sample.csv (short window telemetry export)
- finexa-security-questions.pdf (your SOC/compliance questionnaire)

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Technical deep-dive (model shape, prompt lengths, batching opportunities) — aditya_rao to lead. Suggested times: Thu 3/4 or Fri 3/5, 10–11am PT.
2) Redwood to run a quick capacity estimate based on your telemetry — kimberly_park to share baseline numbers by 3/4.
3) Security & compliance touchpoint to confirm KMS/HSM requirements — laura_bennett to coordinate with your security team, target week of 3/8.
4) Draft mutual action plan with milestone for pilot (2-week reserved pool) — delivery by 3/9.

Please reply with confirmation for the deep-dive slot and any adjustments to the success criteria above.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0136
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns well with what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Predictable throughput: our 500 RPS burst target is important for promotional days; if Redwood can guarantee burst-to-2x baseline with a short ramp and clear pricing, that would be ideal.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms is right for interactive widgets; for longer contextual completions we can accept p95 < 500ms.
- Isolation: we need both dedicated GPU tenancy and the option to run private control plane in our VPC (we will provide an initial network diagram).

Deep-dive: Thu 3/4 10:00am PT works for our engineering lead (I'll invite her). We'll attach a sanitized telemetry export (sensitive fields redacted) ahead of the meeting.

Also attaching the security questionnaire (we've started filling page 2).

—Daniel
